description: Dark as bog oak, black grain running through the brown. A felled Sprigling's last: it stiffens plate and hands blows back.
lore: It will not take a polish and it will not be forced. There is grain in it, black under the brown, turning at a knot the way sawn oak turns, and an armourer sets a plate across the run of it or watches the first real blow start a split that does not stop. No other stone asks to be read first. Most of the trade finds that quietly insulting.

Worn right, it keeps a ledger: a share of every blow goes back to whoever gave it, at once, at about the size it was given, and the wearer feels nothing at all. Two exchanges in, the other party is usually looking at their own hands. Not protection — bookkeeping.

[[characters/54bead23|Osric]] ruined his first one the week he bought it, taking a smith's hammer to a thing that wanted a joiner's patience, and the two halves are nailed up over his forge door. Ask why he keeps them and you get the whole of what he will so far say about being dead: some things here are worked with, not on. Then he reads the next [[monsters/forest_poring_2|Sprigling]] stone a long while before touching it, like a man laying a floor.
